sourceObservations: Recognizable compact timber workshop with alternating cyan/blue roof strips, navy ridge, short chimney, small golden window and one front door. The S image is the original snapshot; all four published source atlases are available at 384x896.

The roof dominates S/N silhouettes; its thin flat strips, very straight ridge and saturated near-unmodulated cyan make it read assembled from rigid bars. E/W reveal a pitched roof but long blank dark side walls and abrupt underside transitions.

The front door is a flat plain panel with a very small knob; the small bright window reads but its surrounding construction is minimally articulated. Back/side walls have large undifferentiated brown regions.

Native source contains the named S33_PROP_workshop-hut.001 collection, workshop-hut__root.001, 29 evaluated mesh parts, independent materials and no hut armature. Source root has identity transform, one-cell support footprint and the local semantic door socket [-0.12,-0.56,0].

Evaluated source mesh envelope is X [-0.583000004,0.583000004], Y [-0.609985411,0.609985411], Z [0.024999976,1.804999948]. Roof overhang is larger than the nominal one-cell body occupancy. The 1.81 visual-height declaration matches this upper envelope within 0.005.

Source materials are native shader graphs; current world lighting is four equal 100 W cardinal area fills and one centered 140 W overhead. Own diagnostic captures retain those source materials/lights/compositor. Large dark side/rear wall regions need visible form and warm material separation in the refined treatment.

The blend opens with a character camera and character render dimensions. I rebuilt the hut-specific camera from the hut source-camera record in memory: root [192,704], X unit [256,0], depth unit approximately [0,256], height unit approximately [0,-179.2] in a 384x896 frame. The saved active camera was not used as hut evidence.

The source collection was excluded/hidden in its saved view layer. The valid evaluated audit explicitly enables its layer and object visibility before measuring/rendering. The two early inventory files contain stale identity mesh matrices and are not placement authorities. The final evaluated record and actual nonempty native captures supersede those fields.

Own 2x diagnostic native rasters and published 2x rasters show the same construction but differ by approximately two native pixels at alpha edges, consistent with an unresolved historical capture/downsample pipeline difference. No exact source-raster reproduction claim is made. The historical 4x metadata does not prove the present raw-frame bytes are available.
targetObservations: The fixed target adds substantial rounded roof volume, broad pale bevel highlights, a stronger navy ridge with end caps and warm brass fasteners, and a chimney built from a cap and a lower collar. These are useful native reconstruction goals rather than fixed part counts.

Warm honey timber, recessed plank seams, substantial darker corner posts, framed glowing window and a visibly crafted door give the target a more inviting and deliberate construction. Door hinge straps and a ring handle supply purposeful workshop detail.

The target uses a dominant cool roof against a warm timber body. Soft continuous form shading and bright but bounded edge accents are the strongest style cues; its left/right edge variation must not become a preferred horizontal light direction in a rotatable asset.

The target is 820x1918 and has shifted/scaled silhouette relative to the registered source. Its transparent fringe contains cyan/red flecks; those are generation artifacts to reject. It supplies front design/style guidance, not camera, ground contact, doorway dimensions, registration or unseen N/E/W geometry authority.
styleReferenceObservations: The plant reference has clear large volumes, warm golden container edges, saturated but separated colors, softened corner highlights and readable shaded planes. Preserve those qualities while avoiding the bright yellow/green alpha fringe visible around the reference.

The hut should feel crafted and softly lit, with a readable roof, walls, trim and door at logical use size. Added detail should support those large forms rather than replace them with high-frequency noise.
initialPriorities: Reconstruct a convincing thick pitched roof and timber hut with softened volumes and useful structural detail, within the registered physical envelope and gameplay contacts.
Retain cyan/blue, warm wood, navy trim and golden light while improving material/form separation under horizontally neutral soft lighting.
Keep readable warm side/back construction and clean alpha edges in every facing; avoid black wall dead spots, intersections, bright halos and cast ground shadows.
